findings.finding: Company guide math leaves room for a fourth straight raise or a narrowing up. FY2026 FFO As Adjusted is guided at $1.24-1.26, raised at Q1 (from $1.21-1.25) and again at Q2 (low end up from $1.22). H1 actual is $0.61, implying H2 of $0.63-0.65, while the Q3 consensus of $0.31 and the FY consensus of $1.24 sit at or below the bottom of that implied path. Management said same-property NOI is tracking above the midpoint of its 5-9% range after 8.7% in Q2, and the signed-not-open pipeline is a record $16.5m (about $0.01 of FFO in H2 2026). Against this, management flagged about a penny of drag from investment-management sales before redeployment, which is already inside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed the midpoint or top of the guide, FY consensus would sit at $1.25 or above rather than $1.24, and the stock would not be down about 17% since a print that raised guidance. The EW preview explicitly reads the bottom-of-range consensus as Street doubt about the upper half.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 release documents the earlier raise and the $0.30 Q1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899629/000119312526187104/akr-ex99_1.htm). The EW preview carries the SNO, same-property NOI tracking and penny-of-dilution commentary from the Q2 call (https://finviz.com/news/407858/acadias-record-leasing-story-meets-a-17-stock-slide-ahead-of-q3-results). Both are company-sourced, so this is one line of evidence.

findings.finding: Intra-quarter operating evidence from the company's 2026-09-14 update: about $119m of REIT street-retail acquisitions quarter-to-date (Greene St SoHo $60m, Bleecker $20m, Greenwich Ave $10m, Melrose $29m). It reports 12 new leases with $4.8m ABR quarter-to-date, street-retail new leases and renewals at double-digit cash spreads, and 129 Fifth Ave leased within 30 days of closing above underwriting, at a yield on cost above 9%. It reiterates the $400-500m street-acquisition target and says no new equity was issued quarter-to-date. JLL's Q3 2026 Manhattan prime data (2026-10-07) independently shows SoHo availability at a record low of 7.4% and SoHo ground-floor asking rent up 25.6% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Leasing and same-property NOI strength (Q2 street retail same-property NOI +15.6%, 91% new-lease spreads) bought +2.21% on 2026-07-28, then the stock gave back about 17% over three months, so strong operating data has not held.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the update was public six weeks ago. The JLL SoHo series is a broad independent read on Acadia's core corridor, and if it were priced the stock would not be trading near its 52-week low with record corridor tightness. Most of this is public, so the size is small.
findings.independence: JLL Q3 2026 via CRE Daily (https://www.credaily.com/?p=223702, 2026-10-07) is a different source from the company update, and CBRE Q3 2026 Manhattan retail figures show average corridor asking rent up 5% y/y (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/manhattan-retail-figures-q3-2026).

findings.finding: Short interest is 10.0% of float with 10.4 days to cover (FINRA record date 2026-10-15), elevated for a REIT, though down 4.9% from the prior report and from about 12-13% in summer. A clean print with a reaffirmed or raised guide meets a short base that takes about two weeks of volume to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has been visible in the last seven prints: the maximum absolute reaction is 4.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Shorts are already covering (-4.9%), so part of the cover is done. The size is small because 10% of float is well below the 18-23% squeeze cases.
findings.independence: equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/akr/shortinterest) gave 12.3% of float and 12.6 days to cover in August, the same series at an earlier date.

findings.finding: Peer guide raises landed after Acadia last spoke. Brixmor (2026-10-26) raised FY2026 Nareit FFO to $2.36-2.38 from $2.35-2.37, with Q3 same-property NOI +6.6% and record 95.6% leased occupancy. Federal Realty (2026-10-30, bmo) raised Core FFO to $7.54-7.58 from $7.48-7.56 and adjusted comparable POI growth to 4.375-4.625% from 4.0-4.5%. Both point to an intact retail-REIT leasing backdrop for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific history: this is a sector read-across.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, and largely priced at the sector level: FRT reported this morning and its move sits in the sealed spot. Acadia's street-retail mix differs from grocery-anchored peers, so the transmission is weak and the size small.
findings.independence: Federal Realty Q3 2026 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000034903/000003490326000054/frt-9302026xex991.htm), a different company and document.

findings.finding: The stock is down about 17% since the 2026-07-28 print against S&P +2.7% (EW preview, 2026-10-26), with no company-specific negative in EDGAR. The only filings since are a trustee appointment 8-K (2026-10-19), the related Form 3/4 and passive 13Gs. Expectations into the print are low: EW says sentiment moved from mildly bullish to neutral, and the stock sits below its 200-day moving average ($20.67).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the guide-raising Q2 print (+2.21%) the stock slid steadily, which says this shareholder base has not paid for good operating news over a multi-week horizon.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the market's pricing. The finding is that the bar has been lowered without a company-level cause, so a reaffirmation can clear it. Absence of an explanation is weak evidence: the slide may reflect rates or concern over funding $400-500m of acquisitions with forward equity. Sized near zero for that reason.
findings.independence: The EDGAR filing list shows only a trustee 8-K and 13Gs since 2026-07-29 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000899629&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). The 8-K exhibit is a board appointment with no business data (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/899629/000119312526425260/akr-ex99_1.htm).

findings.finding: Funding and dilution offsets. Management guided about a penny of drag from investment-management sales before proceeds are redeployed, and street acquisitions are funded by settling about $352m of remaining forward equity (17.8m shares at the Q2 release) at roughly 1.9x equity multiple exits. The goal of $1bn of street acquisitions 'by year-end' (EW) or the $400-500m annual REIT target ($318m done by 09-14) leaves a Q4 gap. A Q3 or Q4 FFO cadence that leans on future accretion could keep the guide top-heavy, or lead to it being narrowed at the bottom instead of raised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The initial FY2026 guide (2026-02-10), where growth was seen as back-end-loaded, sold -4.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management disclosed the dilution and the forward equity is known. Following lesson 4, the financing buys visible street-retail acquisitions with above-underwriting leasing, so it is not distress. The negative is only the timing of accretion. Small.
findings.independence: The Sept 14 update confirms the forward-settlement funding and $352m remaining (https://finviz.com/news/391570/acadia-realty-trust-provides-investment-balance-sheet-and-leasing-update). It shares the company as source.

outside_window.finding: The signed-not-open pipeline ($16.5m ABR) is guided to add $0.03-0.05 of FFO in 2027 and the rest in 2028. The street mark-to-market is about 25% below market ($20-25m of rent). Both are multi-year, though a first 2027 view on the call could carry part of this inside the window.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive against a 17% drawdown, a 20-day run-up of only +2.4% and no option skew to read. They cut against the price trend, not against a stated option lean, and a muted reaction history (raises bought about +2%) keeps p_up at 57 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown and 'no filing' are not a cause): the 17%-slide/low-bar finding went from +0.5 to +0.2.
Rule 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): the guide finding went from +0.8 to +0.6, because the penny of IM-sale dilution management flagged sits inside the same guide.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest at 10% of float and falling is not the 18-23% squeeze case, so the short-interest finding went from +0.4 to +0.3.
Rule 5 (proxy): the BRX/FRT peer raises went from +0.3 to +0.2 as sector transmission the company has not confirmed.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): the forward equity buys street acquisitions with above-underwriting leasing, so the funding/dilution negative went from -0.3 to -0.2, a timing item rather than distress.
Rule 1: left the scaled number unchanged (p_up 57, abs 2.8), since the muted reaction history was already applied to p_up in the draft.
